newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Grains-Big sales highlight week. [CORRECTED 20:14 GMT 16/12]
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Grains-Big sales highlight week. [CORRECTED 20:14 GMT 16/12]

text.p: The Australian grains industry was dominated last week by a one million tonne sale of wheat to India and a 225,00 tonne wheat sale to Pakistan.
The sales are seen providing Australia with a potential competitive edge in the run-up to next year's northern hemisphere new crop.

"The (Indian) contract calls on us to to ship during January and February to an already very busy early shipping programme, with shipments divided between east and west coast ports," the AWB's international general manager Nigel Officer said.
It will reduce the storage costs on a big crop and the amount of wheat Australia will be looking to sell against the northern crop, he said.

AWB analyst Alex Nicol told Reuters it was inevitable that with expectations of a crop in excess of 21 million tonnes this year -- the largest since 1982/83 -- Ausralia would have more wheat to sell next year.

Activity in the the physical export market was in contrast to only slight volatility at the Sydney Futures Exchange, where nearby January wheat settled little changed on the week at A$165.00 a tonne, while March fetched A$163.00 a tonne.
Traders attributed the light volumes in part to little interest among growers to come to the market despite the bumper crop.
In a more dynamic physical export market, the Pakistan sale was carried via tender using commodities trader Cargill, while the India transaction was a direct sale.
Wheat to India is reportedly to be shipped in 50,000-tonnes lots at a price of around A$185 a tonne, which is line with current AWB pool estimates.
The Australian Wheat Board also gave notice last week that it intended to compete vigorously with the U.S. and other countries in future tenders.

"We've been invited to tender... for the January (Pakistan) cargo and we will be submitting a price and hopefully it will be competitive," Mark Emons, AWB regional manager of international marketing, told Reuters.

The Pakistani Ministry of Food and Agriculture has invited bids later this month for the supply of 270,000 tonnes U.S. Grade-2 or better soft white wheat to be financed under an export credit guarantee programme.
Canada is seen by traders as a likely candidate to fulfill all or part of India's remaining one-million tonne requirement.
The Canadian Wheat Board (CWB) has indicated it has wheat for sale and is in talks with India.

"The price of Canadian wheat would have to be below the CWB's initial price (a government partial payment) to compete, which could be below US$150.00 a tonne," a trade source told Reuters in Winnipeg. (Corrects attribution)
Benchmark No1 Canada Western Red Spring Wheat's initial price is C$190 a tonne, in-store Vancouver, or US$139.78
